newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close lower, pork bellies sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close lower, pork bellies sharply higher.

text.p: CME hog futures closed lower amid signs the recent run-up in the cash market may be running out of steam while bellies finished sharply up.
Dealers said Cargill and E.D. and F. Man International were featured sellers of August hogs late while Rand Financial Services' commercial desk was a big seller on the day.

Cash hogs were expected to sell steady to weak on Wednesday after climbing between $1.00 and $1.50 at interior markets during the first couple of days this week as hot, humid weather slowed hog marketings in the U.S. Midwest.
"It (the cash market rise) was overdone," one dealer said.
Dealers said Iowa Grain was a noted seller of October hogs while ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp was a featured buyer.
August hogs ended off 0.175 cent per lb at 80.975 cents with other months down 0.650 to 0.150 cent. July hogs expired around midday, finishing 0.025 cent up at 83.725 cents.
Pork belly futures closed sharply higher, boosted by a strong cash market with LFG and E.D. and F. Man International the big buyers on the day, floor sources said.
Cash bellies were quoted $2.00 per cwt higher on Tuesday, as of 1115 CDT, for 12- to 14-lb supplies, according to USDA. The rise follows a $2.00 increase on Monday.

The CME's weekly out-of-town pork belly storage report, issued after the close, showed a slightly smaller than expected net out-movement of 2.124 million lbs from CME-approved warehouses outside Chicago.
August pork belly futures closed 2.525 cent a lb higher at 82.775 cents with other months up 2.925 to 1.100 cents.
